# SIM-046 fixtures: coverage queries, options, database and control API

Run by [`tests/sim_feature_completion/sim_046.rs`](../../../../sim_feature_completion/sim_046.rs).
Positive cases run in both optimizer modes on the legacy, compact/portable and
compact/GMP value backends; error and negative cases run in both optimizer
modes. Line numbers refer to the `pdftotext -layout` extraction
`SystemVerilog-1800-2009.txt` (SV). The interpretations that needed a choice
are the register decisions
[S46-D1 and later](../../../../../docs/lrm_decisions.md#coverage-queries-database-and-control-sim-046).

## Clauses relied on

- 19.7, L33340-33344: "Option assignment statements in the covergroup
  definition are evaluated at the time that the covergroup is instantiated.
  The per_instance and get_inst_coverage options can only be set in the
  covergroup definition. The auto_bin_max and detect_overlap options can only
  be set in the covergroup or coverpoint definition. Other instance-specific
  options can be assigned procedurally after a covergroup has been
  instantiated."
- 19.7 Table 19-1, L33265-33267: "name=string unique name Specifies a name for
  the covergroup instance. If unspecified, a unique name for each instance is
  automatically generated by the tool."
- 19.7, L33358-33363: "All instance options can be specified at the
  covergroup level. Except for the weight, goal, comment, and per_instance
  options, all other options set at the covergroup syntactic level act as a
  default value for the corresponding option of all coverpoints and crosses
  in the covergroup. Individual coverpoints or crosses can overwrite these
  default values."
- 19.7.1, L33491-33492: "The strobe type option can only be set in the
  covergroup definition. Other type options can be assigned procedurally at
  any time during simulation."
- 19.8 Table 19-5, L33553-33560: "real get_coverage() ... real
  get_coverage(ref int, ref int) ... real get_inst_coverage() ... real
  get_inst_coverage(ref int, ref int) ... void set_inst_name(string) ... Sets
  the instance name to the given string".
- 19.8, L33584-33595: "When the optional arguments are specified, the
  get_coverage() and get_inst_coverage() methods assign to the first argument
  the number of covered bins and to the second argument the number of
  coverage bins defined for the given coverage item. When
  get_inst_coverage() is called on a coverpoint or cross, these two values
  correspond to the numerator and the denominator used for calculating the
  particular coverage number ... When get_inst_coverage() is called on a
  covergroup, these values are aggregated numbers of bins from all
  constituent coverpoints and crosses of the same instance. When
  get_coverage() is called on a coverpoint or cross, these values are
  aggregated numbers of bins from the same coverpoint or cross in all
  instances. When get_coverage() is called on a covergroup, these values are
  aggregated numbers of bins from all coverpoints and crosses in all
  instances."
- 19.9, L33683-33688: "$set_coverage_db_name ( filename ) sets the filename
  of the coverage database into which coverage information is saved at the
  end of a simulation run. $load_coverage_db ( filename ) loads from the given
  filename the cumulative coverage information for all coverage group types.
  $get_coverage ( ) returns as a real number in the range of 0 to 100 the
  overall coverage of all coverage group types."
- 19.10, L33696-33754: the `option` members `string name; int weight; int
  goal; string comment; int at_least; int auto_bin_max; int
  cross_num_print_missing; bit detect_overlap; bit per_instance; bit
  get_inst_coverage;` and the `type_option` members `int weight; int goal;
  string comment; bit strobe; bit merge_instances;`.
- 19.11, L33768-33769: "The coverage of a coverage group, Cg , is the
  weighted average of the coverage of all items defined in the coverage
  group".
- 19.11.3, L33937-33940: "When type_option.merge_instances is false, type
  coverage is computed as the weighted average of all instances. When
  type_option.merge_instances is true, type coverage is computed as if
  instances were merged together into the type, as a union of coverage of all
  instances."
- 19.11.3, L33959-33962: "the union of all bins from all instances must be
  computed. To determine when bins overlap among instances, the bin name is
  used ... the cumulative coverage count of an overlapping bin is the sum of
  counts of that bin in all instances containing it."
- Table 19-1, L33291-33295: "get_inst_coverage=boolean 0 Only applies when
  the merge_instances type option is set. ... When false, the value returned
  by get_inst_coverage shall equal the value returned by get_coverage."

- 40.2.2, L66035-66036: "assertion coverage: For each assertion, whether it
  has had at least one success."
- 40.3.1, L66077-66100: the constants `SV_COV_START 0`, `SV_COV_STOP 1`,
  `SV_COV_RESET 2`, `SV_COV_CHECK 3`, `SV_COV_MODULE 10`, `SV_COV_HIER 11`,
  `SV_COV_ASSERTION 20`, `SV_COV_FSM_STATE 21`, `SV_COV_STATEMENT 22`,
  `SV_COV_TOGGLE 23`, `SV_COV_OVERFLOW -2`, `SV_COV_ERROR -1`,

- 40.3.2.5, L66352-66360: "Saving coverage shall not have any effect on the

- 40.5.3, L66612-66652: the attempt, nonvacuous success (cover sequence:
  match), vacuous success, disabled ("as a result of disable iff condition
  becoming true or if an attempt starts when the disable iff is true"),
  killed and failure counts, and "in progress = attempts - (successes +
  vacuous success + disabled + killed + failures)".

## options.sv

Group `g`: `p` has bins `lo` {0..3}, `mid` {4..7}, `hi` {8..15}
(type_option.weight 2); `q` has `z` {0} and `o` {1}; `x` crosses them,
3 x 2 = 6 products. Instances `a` and `b`.

- `names`: the default names `tb.g#1`, `tb.g#2` (S46-D1: unique; llg's form is
  `<declaration scope>.<group>#<creation order>`).
- `comments`: the declared `option.comment`s ("g instance", "p", none for
  `q`) and `type_option.comment` "g type".
- `type`: type_option weight 1, goal 90 (declared), `p` weight 2, `q` weight 1,
  merge_instances 0.
- `defaults`: Table 19-1 defaults 1, 100, 1, 64, 0, 0, 0, 0.
- `written`: the writes read back; `a.q.option.at_least` stays 1 because only
  `a.p` was written.
- Samples: `a` gets (1,0), (2,0), (5,1); `b` gets (9,1).
  - `a.p` (at_least 2): lo 2 hits (covered), mid 1 (not), hi 0: 1/3,
    33.333333. `a.q`: z 2, o 1: 2/2. `a.x`: (lo,z) 2, (mid,o) 1: 2/6,
    33.333333. `a`: (33.333333 + 100 + 33.333333) / 3 = 55.555556; bins
    1+2+2 = 5 of 3+2+6 = 11.
  - `b`: p hi 1/3, q o 1/2, x (hi,o) 1/6: (33.333333 + 50 + 16.666667) / 3 =
    33.333333; 3 of 11.
  - `type` (merge_instances 0, instance weights 3 and 1): (3 x 55.555556 +
    33.333333) / 4 = 50.0; bins summed over instances, 8 of 22 (19.8).
  - `type.p`: (33.333333 + 33.333333) / 2 with coverpoint weights 1; 2 of 6.
  - `merged` (merge_instances 1): p: lo 2 (covered), mid 1 and hi 1 (the
    largest at_least of the instances, 2, is not reached; S45-D18): 1/3.
    q: z 2, o 2: 2/2. x: (lo,z), (mid,o), (hi,o): 3/6. Weighted by the item
    type weights 2, 1, 1: (2 x 33.333333 + 100 + 50) / 4 = 54.166667; 6 of
    11 merged bins (S46-D7).
  - `merged a`: get_inst_coverage is 0, so it equals get_coverage (Table
    19-1). `$get_coverage()` with one type is that type's coverage.
  - `unmerged`: back to 50.0 after the procedural write.
- `renamed`: set_inst_name and the `option.name`/`option.comment` and
  `type_option.comment` writes.

## database.sv

Three runs in one directory. `g` (at_least 2 via the declaration) has
`b[4]` over 0..15 (b[0] 0..3, b[1] 4..7, b[2] 8..11, b[3] 12..15);
instances `one`, `two` (and `three` in the second run) named by
`option.name = tag`. `h` (merge_instances 1) has `q` (lo/hi) and `tr`
(`up = (1 => 2)`).

- `+first`: one: b[0] 1, b[1] 1: 0/4. two: b[3] 2: 1/4. g = (0 + 25) / 2 =
  12.5, bins 1 of 8. h (m: 1, 2): q lo 1/2, tr up 1/1: 75.0, 2 of 3.
  `$get_coverage` = (12.5 + 75) / 2 = 43.75. Saved to cov.db at the end.
- `+second` after `$load_coverage_db("cov.db")` (S46-D2): every loaded record
  joins the live instance of the same name, so the numbers equal the first
  run's: `loaded` = `first`; `one` alone is still 0/4 (instance coverage is
  not changed by a load).
  Then one: 1 (b[0]), 6 (b[1]): with the loaded counts b[0] 2 and b[1] 2:
  2/4 = 50. two stays 25. three: 15 (b[3] 1): 0/4. g = (50 + 25 + 0) / 3 =
  25.0, 3 of 12. `one` live alone: b[0] 1, b[1] 1: 0/4. h: m samples 9 (hi);
  merged with the loaded record: q 2/2, tr 1/1: 100.0, 3 of 3. Total (25 +
  100) / 2 = 62.5. Saved to cov2.db.
- `+third` loads cov2.db: one (live, unsampled) with its loaded record 50,
  two 25, the loaded `three` alone 0: 25.0, 3 of 12; h 100. Loading cov2.db a
  second time adds every count again (loaded records with the same name and
  layout merge by addition): three's b[3] reaches 2: 25; g = (50 + 25 + 25)
  / 3 = 33.333333, 4 of 12; total (33.333333 + 100) / 2 = 66.666667. The
  third run names no database, so it saves nothing (S46-D3).

## db_errors.sv

`g` has one automatic coverpoint over `bit [W-1:0] v`, W = 4: 16 bins; one
sample of 3: 1/16 = 6.25. The test saves good.db, then builds damaged copies
in Rust from the documented format (`src/sim/rt/coverage/database.c`) and
loads each with `+load=bad.db`:

| Case | Message | Output |
| --- | --- | --- |
| two valid records (good.db's and a copy named `other1` counting bin 5) | none | 2 of 32 bins: two members of 1/16 |
| first 30 bytes | the file is not an llg coverage database | unchanged 1/16 |
| one bit flipped | the checksum does not match | unchanged |
| foreign magic | the file is not an llg coverage database | unchanged |
| `other1`, then a record counting bin 16 of 16 | a counter is outside its bins | unchanged: the valid first record is not published either |
| good.db read by the W = 3 model | it was saved by a model with different covergroups | 1/8 = 12.5 of the narrower model |
| missing.db, and saving to `nodir/x.db` | was not loaded / was not saved | no database and no temporary file left |

Every failed load or save is a run-time error: the run exits with status 1.

## assertions.sv

Assertion coverage counters, scopes and control in two runs (the second
with `+merge`). Posedge k of `clk` is at time 10k - 5; the values that
posedge k samples are set at time 10(k - 1). `unit` has `p: a |=> b`,
`c: cover a ##1 b` and `s: (a ##1 a) |=> b`, all `disable iff (off)`.

| k | u1 a b | u2 a b off |
| --- | --- | --- |
| 1 | 1 0 | 1 0 0 |
| 2 | 1 1 | 1 0 1 (off2 = 1 at t 10..20) |
| 3 | 0 1 | 1 0 0 |
| 4 | 1 0 | 1 1 0 |
| 5 | 0 0 | 0 0 0 (`$assertkill(0, tb.u2)` at t 40, `$asserton` at t 50) |
| 6-8 | u1 stopped at t 50; 6: 0 0, 7: 1 0, 8: 0 1 | 6: 0 0, 7: 1 0, 8: 0 1 |

Counters (attempts, successes, vacuous, failures, disabled, killed), in
table (elaboration) order; the test reads them from `acov.db`:

- `checks::check.pk` (owned by `$root`, S46-D9): values -1, 0, 1, 2:
  (4, 3, 0, 1, 0, 0).
- `u1.p` (ticks 1-5 before the STOP): 1 -> b(2) success, 2 -> b(3)
  success, 3 vacuous, 4 -> b(5) = 0 failure (the message at 45000), 5
  vacuous: (5, 2, 2, 1, 0, 0). `u1.c`: matches 1-2 and 2-3; 4-5 does not
  match, which is no failure (S46-D8): (5, 2, 0, 0, 0, 0). `u1.s`: 1-2
  matches the antecedent, b(3) = 1 succeeds; 2 (a(3) = 0), 3, 4 (a(5) = 0)
  and 5 are vacuous: (5, 1, 4, 0, 0, 0). Ticks 6-8 count nothing: u1 is
  stopped.
- `u2.p`: 1 pending, disabled when off2 rises at t 10; 2 starts while off2
  holds: an attempt, disabled; 3 -> b(4) success; 4 pending, killed at t
  40; 5 none (killed assertions are off until `$asserton`); 6 vacuous; 7 ->
  b(8) success; 8 vacuous: (7, 2, 2, 0, 2, 1). `u2.c` likewise, with 6 and
  8 non-matches: (7, 2, 0, 0, 2, 1). `u2.s`: 1 disabled, 2 disabled; 3
  matches its antecedent at 4 and waits for b(5); 4 waits for a(5): both
  killed; 6, 8 vacuous, 7 vacuous at 8 (a(8) = 0): (7, 0, 3, 0, 2, 2).
- `tb.cs` (cover sequence a1 ##1 b1, never stopped): ticks 1-8, matches
  1-2, 2-3, 7-8: (8, 3, 0, 0, 0, 0).
- `tb.im` (x = -1..2, fails for 1), `tb.ic` (x == 2), `tb.dc` (deferred,
  x == 0): (4, 3, 0, 1, 0, 0), (4, 1, 0, 0, 0, 0), (4, 1, 0, 0, 0, 0).
- `tb.im2` is checked once: the first pass runs under `$assertoff`
  (S46-D8): (1, 0, 0, 1, 0, 0).

Queries (covered/items, S46-D4: an item with a nonvacuous success):
`tb` HIER holds 11 items (3 + 3 + cs, im, ic, dc, im2), `u1` MODULE 3,
`u2` HIER 3, `"unit"` MODULE 6 (both instances), `$root` MODULE 1 (pk) and
`tb` MODULE 5.

- start: nothing covered.
- tick 5 (t 50): u1 3/3, u2 2/3 (s has no success), cs covered: tb 6/11,
  unit 5/6, top 1/5.
- tick 8: unchanged (u1 stopped; u2's p and c were already covered).
- checks: pk, im, ic, dc covered: tb 9/11, root 1/1, top 4/5.
- `$coverage_save` writes `acov.db` (OK); RESET of `u2` HIER zeroes its
  three items: tb 7/11, u2 0/3, unit 3/6.
- Second run: `$coverage_merge` adds `acov.db` (OK), so 9 items are covered
  at the start; the run counts the same again, and `acov2.db` holds twice
  every counter above (the save precedes the RESET in both runs).

## control.sv

Status values of Table 40-1 and the scopes of Table 40-2. `tb` has `m1` and
`m2` (`mid`, each with `leaf l` holding `lp`) and `e` (`empty_unit`, no
assertion).

- CHECK: `tb` HIER 1 (two items below); `tb` MODULE 0 (tb owns none); `m1.l`
  MODULE 1; `"mid"` HIER 1; `"mid"` MODULE 0 (mid owns none); `$root` HIER 1.
- `e`: CHECK 0, START 0 (no coverage), STOP 1, RESET 1 (no effect), get 0,
  max 0 (S46-D12).
- Errors (-1): control 4, type 19, type 24, scope_def 12, the unknown
  definition `"nosuch"`, the instance name `"m1"` as a string (S46-D6), an
  all-x type, a save of type 19, a STOP with scope_def 9.
- Kinds 21-23 (S46-D5): CHECK 0, START 0, STOP 1, RESET 1, get 0, max 0,
  save 0; `never.db` is not written.
- After tick 1: covered 2/2. A RESET of `m1` HIER written as a statement
  zeroes `m1.l.lp`: 1. `c.db` saved (OK); merging it as toggle coverage
  returns 0 (found, no toggle data), as assertion coverage 1: m2's success
  is added again, m1 still has none: 1.

## merge_errors.sv

`N` generate blocks each hold `ap: assert property (1)`. One tick before
`+save`: each item (1, 1, 0, 0, 0, 0).

| Case | Status | Message |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `+merge=good.db` | 1, covered 2/2 at time 0; `two.db` holds (2, 2, 0, 0, 0, 0) | none |
| good.db merged by the N = 3 model | -1, 0/3 | it was saved by a model with different assertions |
| one bit flipped | -1 | the checksum does not match (the file is corrupt) |
| a valid frame and hash with an item table of one item | -1 | the assertion section does not match its item table |
| a functional-only database (`db_errors`) | 0 (NOCOV) | none |
| good.db merged as toggle coverage | 0 (NOCOV) | none |
| `missing.db` as assertion and as toggle coverage | -1, -1 | was not merged: (system reason) |

After each failed merge `after.db` holds the run's own counters only. A
failed merge is a run-time error: exit status 1 (S46-D11).

## final_query.sv

`final` procedures run after `$finish` and still query live records: the
instance has `lo` hit, 1/2 = 50.00 (instance, type and total); `ap` succeeded
at tick 1: 1/1; the save returns OK.
